A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, equations, Figures 1–13, Table 1 and Appendices A–E. All ten appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v4 reports original random-matrix simulations and trained-network experiments on synthetic manifolds, MNIST, Cifar10 and CelebA, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v6 retains these original simulations and network measurements in Sections 7–8 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The score models, training objectives and spectral estimation procedures remain unchanged, including the orthogonalized and central-difference procedures in Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic linear manifolds, nonlinear ellipsoid example, MNIST, Cifar10 and CelebA. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 4 retains the analytical-versus-learned spectra comparison. Figure 9 retains the comparison between Stanczuk et al.'s standard SVD procedure and the orthogonalized procedure, with unchanged comparator membership.

E3.justification: Table 1 and Appendices B–C retain identical model configurations, training budgets, sample sizes, normalization and spectral measurement procedures. Figure settings and evaluation times also match.

E4.justification: The variance experiments in Figure 3, estimation-method comparison in Figure 9, nonlinear-manifold check in Figure 10 and individual-image analyses in Figures 11–13 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 realizations of the projection matrix for Figures 2 and 7. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted results and reported findings match throughout, including the theory/network comparison in Figure 4 and the estimated MNIST manifold dimension of approximately 100 in Section 8.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, spectral-gap formulas and appendix derivations are unchanged. Section 3 replaces p(x_t, t) with the equivalent notation p_t(x_t); Section 6's revised introduction names the same previously analyzed distributional cases.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and closing discussion retain the same contributions: random-matrix analysis of diffusion geometry, experimental spectral analysis, three geometric phases and an explanation of avoiding manifold overfitting.

C2.justification: The manifold-overfitting explanation, interpretation of the theory/network discrepancy, natural-image discussion and arguments about applicability to curved manifolds remain unchanged, including Appendix D.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain identical architecture, hyperparameter, training-data, hardware and implementation disclosures. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Song/Yang, Wang/Peng and Brooks/Tim labels match the same respective paper titles across versions; these are bibliographic edits rather than changes in cited literature.

P1.justification: v6 removes the standalone Section 6.2 heading, incorporates its revised paragraph into Section 6.1 and renumbers subsequent subsections. It also updates affiliations and equal-contribution marks, adds acknowledgements and edits bibliography formatting and author metadata.

P2.justification: The author block and phase descriptions are reformatted, equations and figures shift relative to surrounding prose, and references reflow. Figure contents, Table 1 and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged. Limited organizational refinements accompany introduced reference errors: v4's 'Cresswell, J. C.' becomes 'J., C. C.' and 'Mézard, M.' becomes 'Mézard, .' in v6. These malformed author entries produce a small net decline in bibliographic accuracy.
